source_text: Multifarie multisque modis Deus locutus est patribus in prophetis. Aliquando ineffabilia sacramenta docet; aliquando de Salvatore instruit; interdum mores corrigit. Totus psalmus trigesimus sextus moralis est — cura et medicina humanae animae. Principium: Noli aemulari inter malignantes, neque aemulatus fueris facientes iniquitatem; quoniam sicut fenum cito arescent, et sicut olera herbarum cito decident.
pass_a_gloss: In many ways and many modes God spoke to the fathers in the prophets. Sometimes he teaches ineffable sacraments; sometimes he instructs about the Savior; sometimes he corrects morals. The whole thirty-sixth psalm is moral — care and medicine of the human soul. Beginning: Do not envy among the malign, nor be envious of those doing iniquity; for like hay they will quickly dry, and like garden herbs they will quickly fall.
pass_b_english: [[God spoke to the fathers by the prophets in many portions and many ways >> Bible:Hebrews 1:1]]. Sometimes the word unveils mysteries, sometimes the Savior’s coming, sometimes it heals conduct. Psalm 36 is wholly moral medicine. Its opening: [[Do not fret because of evildoers, nor envy those who work iniquity; for they will soon wither like grass >> Bible:Psalm 37:1-2]].
